title: Doing scientific investigation
competency: Describe the steps of a scientific investigation and carry out a fair test.

keywords.def: The process by which scientists approach their work: question, research, hypothesis, test, conclude, communicate.
A tentative explanation for a set of observations, with predictions that can be tested.
An experiment where you change only one factor and keep all the others the same.

en.text: Scientists work in steps: ask a question, do background research, make a hypothesis, test it with an experiment, analyse the results and draw a conclusion, then communicate. If the hypothesis is wrong, make a new one and test again.

screens.title: Taller teff
screens.ask: You notice that teff in one field grows taller than in another. What should a scientist do first?
opts: Ask a question she can test
screens.after: Start with a question, like "Does fertiliser make teff grow taller?" Observations lead to questions.

screens.title: Scientific investigation
paras: Science is learning about the world through observation and inquiry.
Scientists form and test hypotheses, gather and analyse data, then report.
This process is called the scientific investigation or scientific method.

screens.title: Figure 1.9: steps in the scientific method
items: Observations lead to a question that can be measured and answered by experiment.
Find information online, in a library or from earlier studies.
A tentative, logical explanation with predictions you can test.
Do an experiment that someone else can repeat. Keep conditions the same.
Do the results support the hypothesis? If not, make a new one.
Share your methods and results so others can check them.

screens.title: Key words
defs: The process by which scientists approach their work: question, research, hypothesis, test, conclude, communicate.
A tentative explanation for a set of observations, with predictions that can be tested.

screens.text: Put the steps of the scientific method in order.
items: Analyse the results and draw a conclusion
screens.why: These are the six steps in Figure 1.9.
screens.clue: It starts with a question and ends with sharing.

opts: A tentative explanation that can be tested
screens.ans: A tentative explanation that can be tested

screens.text: Your results do not support your hypothesis. What do you do?
opts: Make a new hypothesis and test again
Report that the hypothesis was right
screens.ans: Make a new hypothesis and test again

screens.clue: Look at the "Try again" arrow in Figure 1.9.

screens.text: Communicating results lets other scientists check your methods and results.
screens.why: The book says this step allows others to verify your methods and results.

screens.text: Two schools test the same hypothesis and get different results. What does this mean?
opts: The hypothesis may not be supported; check the methods
screens.ans: The hypothesis may not be supported; check the methods
screens.why: If others get different results, they may not support the hypothesis. Scientists compare methods and look for problems.
screens.clue: What does step 6 say about other researchers?

en.text: In a fair test you change only one factor and keep all others the same, and you repeat the experiment. In Example 1.9 a burning candle covered with a gas jar goes out, which shows that air (oxygen) is needed for burning.

screens.title: Candle under a jar
screens.ask: A lit candle is covered with an upside-down glass jar. What happens?
opts: It goes out after a short time
screens.after: It goes out. The flame uses up the oxygen in the jar.

screens.title: Example 1.9: is air needed for burning?
steps: Question: is air necessary for burning?
Research: books say air is necessary for burning.
Hypothesis: air is needed for burning.
Test: light a candle. It keeps burning in fresh air. Cover it with an inverted gas jar: soon it goes out.
Conclusion: the candle used the oxygen in the jar. Air is necessary for burning.
Communicate: report the result in writing or orally.

screens.title: Keep it fair
paras: If you change any factor, keep all the others the same.
Repeat it a few more times to make sure the results are accurate.

screens.title: Key words
defs: An experiment where you change only one factor and keep all the others the same.

screens.text: Activity 1.7 a: you test if sunlight affects bean growth. What must you keep the same in both pots?
screens.why: Only sunlight changes. Everything else stays the same, so the test is fair.
screens.clue: Which one factor are you testing?

screens.text: In the candle experiment, why does the candle go out under the jar?
opts: The oxygen in the jar gets used up
screens.ans: The oxygen in the jar gets used up
screens.why: The candle takes oxygen from the air in the jar. When too little is left, the flame goes out.
screens.clue: What does a flame need from the air?

screens.text: Lemlem tests beans: pot A in sun with water, pot B in the dark with no water. Pot A grows better. What is wrong?
opts: She changed two factors, so it is not a fair test
She should use three pots of sand
screens.ans: She changed two factors, so it is not a fair test
screens.why: Light AND water were different, so she cannot tell which one caused the difference.
screens.clue: How many things were different between the pots?

screens.text: After an experiment, you should repeat it a few times.
screens.why: The book says repeat it a few more times to make sure the results are accurate.

screens.text: Abel wants to know if salt makes water boil faster. Which plan is a fair test?
opts: Two same pots, same amount of water, same stove; add salt to one only
One pot with salt on a big stove, one without on a small stove
Boil salty water once and stop
screens.ans: Two same pots, same amount of water, same stove; add salt to one only
screens.why: Only the salt changes. Pot, water amount and heat stay the same, so any difference comes from the salt.

items.text: a) A bean plant kept in the dark for two weeks will most likely be
opts: greener than one in the sun
items.why: Plants need sunlight to make food; in the dark they grow pale and weak.
items.clue: What do plants need light for?

items.text: b) Wire is coiled around a nail and joined to a battery. The nail
opts: picks up pins: it acts like a magnet
items.ans: picks up pins: it acts like a magnet
items.why: A current in the coil makes the nail an electromagnet.
items.clue: What does current in a coil do?

items.text: c) A leaf from the sun turns blue-black with iodine. This shows the leaf stores
items.why: Iodine turns blue-black with starch. Leaves store extra sugar as starch.
